changelog: Insert a fallback ordering that, as a last resort, prefers cuts after an essential post-nominal modifier rather than between a noun head and that modifier — addresses the primary finding that head+modifier splits are undervalued.
findings: The prompt underrates cuts that separate a finite (main or light) verb from the core complement or predicate that immediately follows it.

The prompt underestimates harm from cutting a noun head away from its immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier (name, apposition, 'named/called' phrase, 'of' PP, or restrictive relative clause).
The prompt treats fronted adjuncts (temporal, locative, conditional, parenthetical) as safe cut points instead of binding them to their governing clause, causing scope or attachment errors.

edits.now: As a last resort, prefer a cut after the end of an immediately following essenti

diagnosis.why: Inserting the fallback made the model avoid splitting noun heads from immediately following post‑nominal modifiers, so cuts that used to fall between head+modifier were instead moved elsewhere (often earlier), producing roughly equal numbers of improvements and degradations and a small net harm concentrated in short/medium pieces (≤5 words). The change therefore traded fixing head+modifier splits for introducing new early cuts that hurt small pieces and enumerations, so overall H_set did not improve.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should respect that repairing head+modifier splits by preferring cuts after the modifier can push cuts into other short spans or break enumerations, so such a fallback must not force additional early cuts in ≤5-word pieces.
